articles.title: Binance targets full reopening of withdrawals by next week
articles.content: Binance is set to restore withdrawals across all networks and assets by the end of next week. This decision comes after recovering 95% of the $6.3 billion lost in the October hack, which the FBI attributes to North Korean actors, though the nation denies any involvement. Binance pledges to fully reimburse affected clients as operations return to normal.

articles.title: US Supreme Court to consider lawsuit over Robinhood's 2021 IPO
articles.content: Robinhood Markets has filed an appeal with the US Supreme Court concerning a class action lawsuit brought forth by investors. The lawsuit claims the company misled investors ahead of its IPO in July 2021 by not revealing how reduced trading volumes would affect their investments. After initially dismissing the case, the 9th Circuit Court of Appeals has reopened it, with Supreme Court deliberations expected by late June.
articles.excerpt: Robinhood Markets has filed an appeal with the US Supreme Court concerning a class action lawsuit brought forth by investors. The lawsuit claims the company misled investors ahead of its IPO in July 2021 by not revealing how reduced trading volumes would affect their investments.

articles.content: According to Goldman Sachs, the S&P 500 index may reach 8,700 points within the next year, despite a decline in tech shares after the midterm elections in the US. They foresee a notable deceleration in global earnings growth by 2027, mainly in the US. Nevertheless, Goldman remains optimistic about equity valuations, indicating good returns are possible, and they have revised ratings for different regions while bracing for increased volatility.

articles.title: Chicago Fed's Goolsbee says on CNBC the Fed needs to guard against demand overheating
articles.content: Chicago Fed president Austan Goolsbee stated that inflation has moved beyond temporary energy and tariff-related price shocks. He highlighted that increased demand from the AI buildout is pushing prices higher across many sectors including health care and services. Goolsbee emphasized the importance of upcoming inflation data for determining the Fed's rate increase pace. He noted that currently, there is no clear path back to the 2% inflation target.
